entrypoints.summary: An authenticated actor permitted to create application links sends an Admin Console client-settings PUT whose JSON baseUrl value uses a javascript: URL.
A user reaches the account applications page or an OpenID Connect error page that renders the persisted application-link value as a link.

negative_controls: A BaseURL outside permitted HTTP(S) schemes should be rejected or absent from rendered href attributes.
The report contains no captured automated regression-test result or post-fix execution result.
observability.positive_marker: An anchor is rendered with href="javascript:alert()" in the account-applications or error-page response.

preconditions: The actor is authenticated and has permission to create application links in client settings.
For the reported master-realm escalation chain, a master-realm administrator follows the error-page Back to Application link and password reset is activated in the master realm.

impact.affected_asset: Victim browser session and, conditionally, the master-realm administrator account and Admin Console.
impact.attacker_capability: An authenticated actor authorized to create application links can plant a JavaScript URL that executes when another user follows a rendered link; the reported highest-privilege outcome additionally requires master-admin interaction and enabled password reset.
impact.security_effect: Stored cross-site scripting through a persisted application-link URL; report-described conditions permit an account-recovery-based escalation to master Admin Console access.

causal_trace.summary: A user with permission to create application links supplies a client BaseURL beginning with the javascript: scheme through an authenticated client-settings PUT.

The BaseURL field accepts arbitrary characters and therefore does not restrict application links to safe URL schemes; the report contrasts AngularJS prefixing unsafe: in the Admin Console with account and error-page paths that do not handle the value safely.
The account-applications and error-page paths render the stored value into anchor href attributes; the report shows href="javascript:alert()" in both resulting HTML contexts.

A victim who follows the rendered application or back link invokes the JavaScript URL. The report describes a conditional chain in which a master-realm admin clicking the error-page back link has their email changed, after which enabled password reset can yield master Admin Console access.

failure.operation: Browser navigation to a persisted javascript: URL emitted in an anchor href

primary_invariant.kind: application-link URL scheme and character constraint
primary_invariant.statement: Persisted client BaseURL values used as navigable links must be restricted to permitted HTTP(S) URL forms and an allowed character set before rendering.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The reported BaseURL parameter accepted arbitrary characters, including a javascript: scheme, and separate account/error-page renderers emitted that stored value as an href.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report supplies the finding, authenticated PUT shape, rendered href evidence, conditional escalation narrative, and recommended validation. No immutable raw Keycloak source file, implementation-level dataflow locator, resolving patch, or independent test-run result is bundled. The master-admin consequence is conditional and is not asserted as universal.

remediation.invariant_restored: Only BaseURL values beginning with https:// or http:// and containing allowlisted characters are accepted, preventing javascript: values from becoming rendered navigation targets.
mitigation_classes: reject invalid BaseURL values before persistence

target.component: Client application-link BaseURL handling and account/error-page link rendering

oracle.channel: HTTP request plus rendered HTML inspection
oracle.expected_negative: After validation, the same BaseURL submission is rejected or cannot result in a rendered javascript: href; valid HTTP(S) BaseURL values remain accepted.
oracle.expected_positive: A pre-remediation authenticated PUT with baseUrl set to javascript:alert() is accepted and the account-applications or error-page HTML contains an anchor with href="javascript:alert()".
